newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seen buying wheat, may be in for corn-trade.
newsitem.headline: Manila seen buying wheat, may be in for corn-trade.

text.p: Philippine flour millers may enter the U.S. wheat market in the coming week as prices are expected to soften due to better harvests in Europe, Australia and Canada, traders said on Monday.
"I will enter the market if prices fall to $4.30 per bushel for U.S. western white wheat and $4.45 per bushel for dark northern spring wheat," one executive at a flour company said.
Traders said other firms were also in the market for at least 21,000 tonnes more of dark northern spring wheat.
"Bumper harvests in major wheat producing countries in the world will eventually push U.S. wheat prices lower from current high levels," said one trader.

Prices for December wheat in Minneapolis, where the Philippines buys most of the staple, slipped five cents to end on Friday at US$4.29-1/4 a bushel. September wheat dropped 10-3/4 to close at $4.46-1/4 a bushel.
The Philippines may also be forced to enter the U.S. corn market soon because of a severe shortfall in its local corn production.
Philippine corn output for calendar 1996 is expected to reach 4.7 million tonnes against expected demand of 5.5 million tonnes, Agriculture Undersecretary Domingo Panganiban said on Friday.
The Philippines bought 250,000 tonnes of corn from the United States and Argentina in March. Most of the grain is consumed as animal feed in the poultry and livestock industry.
A Philippine flour mill bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat last week for prompt delivery, dealers said.
Two other firms bought 18,900 tonnes of western white wheat at $188 to $189 a tonne C&F for October delivery, traders added.
